slides.title: Enter the US in 2027, Amazon-led, and let hard gates decide every further step

paragraphs.text: Enter the US in 2027, Amazon-led, and let hard gates decide every further step
Should Onsoo enter the US market in 2027, and if so, by which route?
For CEO Park Ji-won and the Board · March 2027 board meeting
Prepared November 2026. Evidence base: the planning-team briefing pack only (no outside research).
All company, competitor and market figures in the pack are synthetic benchmark data.

slides.title: Onsoo should enter the US in 2027 through Amazon, not national retail, and fund it step by step against hard gates

paragraphs.text: Onsoo should enter the US in 2027 through Amazon, not national retail, and fund it step by step against hard gates

Answer: yes, enter the US in 2027 with the Amazon-led route (Option A), run as a gated programme. It is the only route that stays inside the board's cash and margin guardrails. Retail-led breaks them on its own numbers, and a Japan scale-up is safe but builds no US business.
The US is worth entering now: the category is growing fast and Onsoo's products already sell there.

US K-beauty skincare grew 17% a year to $3.6B (2021–25), five times faster than the rest of facial skincare. In the Amazon pilot, monthly units nearly doubled in six months (7,400 → 14,000) at 4.5 stars, and 90-day repeat (29%) is close to the 31% benchmark.
Amazon-led is the only route that fits the guardrails; retail-led fails all three financial tests.

Option A's cumulative cash bottoms at −$1.9M to −$3.9M against the $18M cap, and group margin stays at 9.0% or more. Option B bottoms at −$20.8M even on its own assumptions, cuts group margin to 4.5% in 2027, and rests on sell-through and halo assumptions the evidence contradicts. Japan adds just $7M of revenue by 2030.
The binding risk is ad cost: payback by 2030 needs ACoS of 28.6% or less. No route reaches $40M by 2030.

The pilot ran at 28% ACoS, but brands scaling from $5M to $20M have a median of 32%. At 32%, Option A is still −$2.3M at end-2030 and payback slips past 2030. The worst tested case costs $6.4M, about a third of the cap. Option A reaches $26.4M in 2030 and about $40M by 2032.
Approve Option A with hard gates, re-phase the ambition, and replace the 2029 retail trigger.

Fund a $4M peak-cash envelope and review at end-2027 against ACoS ≤28%, revenue ≥$7M and repeat ≥31%. Consider retail only when aided awareness is above 20% and a right-sized plan fits the guardrails. A national retail launch in 2029 would cut group margin to 6.0%.
Source: Onsoo briefing pack (synthetic data); Onsoo option model (appendix). Cash = cumulative US cash flow incl. working capital, 2027–30.

slides.title: We tested the CEO's hypothesis against seven conditions: the Amazon launch holds up, but the 2029 retail step and the 2030 target do not

paragraphs.text: We tested the CEO's hypothesis against seven conditions: the Amazon launch holds up, but the 2029 retail step and the 2030 target do not
What would have to be true
“Launch in the US in 2027 through Amazon, then add specialty beauty retail from 2029 once Amazon sales pass $10M and aided awareness passes 15%.”
1. The US market is large and growing for K-beauty skincare
$3.6B in 2025, up 17% a year since 2021, against 3.5% a year for other facial skincare
2. Onsoo's products sell in the US
Pilot: 64,800 units ($1.56M) in six months; 4.5 stars from 2,140 reviews; repeat 29% vs 31% benchmark
3. Amazon-led stays inside the cash cap and margin floor
Peak cash −$1.9M to −$3.9M across plan and evidence-based cases (cap −$18M); group margin ≥9.0%
Only if ACoS averages ≤28.6% (≤26.9% if duty rises to 25%); pilot 28%, scaling benchmark 32%
Treat 2030 payback as at risk and manage to an ACoS gate.
Replace the 2029 retail trigger: aided awareness above 20%, plus a retail plan that fits the guardrails.
Retail-led fails the cap, payback and margin floor; Japan adds $7M revenue in a market growing 1.5% a year
6. Retail can be added in 2029 at >$10M Amazon sales and >15% awareness
At 10–20% awareness, newcomers sell 3.5 units/door/week (delisting bar 4.0); national retail in 2029 cuts group margin to 6.0%
7. The chosen route reaches $40M revenue by 2030
No route does within the guardrails: A reaches $26.4M; B reaches $37.6M but burns $20.8M
Source: Onsoo briefing pack (synthetic data); §4 (CEO hypothesis); evidence as cited on the following pages.

slides.title: An Amazon unit earns $3–5 after advertising; a retail unit earns $7.55 but has to carry $7.5M a year of retail fixed cost

paragraphs.text: An Amazon unit earns $3–5 after advertising; a retail unit earns $7.55 but has to carry $7.5M a year of retail fixed cost

Fixed retail cost is $7.5M a year ($6.0M national marketing + $1.5M field sales), plus a $0.5M launch fee and $1,100 per door. At 4.5 units/door/week a door earns 234 × $7.55 = $1,766 a year, so about 4,250 doors would be needed just to cover the fixed cost. The plan has 600–1,000.

Advertising is the biggest swing: each 1-point change in ACoS moves contribution by $0.24 a unit, or $0.67M across Option A's 2.81M units (2027–30). The planning team's 25% is below anything observed.
Source: Onsoo briefing pack (synthetic data); Table 4 (per-unit inputs, Rice Ferment Barrier Cream), Table 6 (fixed costs). Hero-SKU economics applied to all SKUs, as the planning team does.

slides.title: Retail-led's gap is structural: no plausible sell-through or halo pays back $7.5M a year of retail fixed cost by 2030

paragraphs.text: Retail-led's gap is structural: no plausible sell-through or halo pays back $7.5M a year of retail fixed cost by 2030
Option B peak cumulative cash 2027–30, $M, by sell-through and Amazon halo
Cost: retail adds $7.5M a year of fixed cost, plus a $0.5M launch fee and $0.66–1.1M of fixtures.
Contribution: retail units earn only $1.1–1.8M a year even at the plan's 4.5 units/door/week, so the layer loses about $6M a year before any halo.
Halo needed: about 1.6× Option A's Amazon volume just to fit the cap, and about 3.1× to pay back by 2030. The plan assumes 1.3×, with no causal evidence (p. 11).
Margin: B's 2027 US operating loss of $8.7M is 2.6 times the $3.3M the group can absorb while holding 8%. This fails in every case.
Within the cap, but fails payback and margin

Every cell fails the payback test (cumulative cash below zero at end-2030) and the 8% group-margin floor in 2027. Even top-quartile sell-through with double the Amazon halo leaves B $11.6M short of payback.

Source: Onsoo briefing pack (synthetic data); Onsoo option model, Option B with ACoS 25% (planning team) and varying sell-through and Amazon halo. Doors 600/600/800/1,000; Amazon units = Option A × halo.

slides.title: Retail-led's volume assumptions are also unsupported: at Onsoo's awareness, newcomers sell 2.6 units per door per week, below the 4.0 delisting bar

paragraphs.text: Retail-led's volume assumptions are also unsupported: at Onsoo's awareness, newcomers sell 2.6 units per door per week, below the 4.0 delisting bar
First-year units per door per week, newcomer skincare brands, by aided awareness

The 4.5 figure comes from the retailer's deck on successful newcomers, a sample of survivors. At Onsoo's awareness the median is 2.6, and even the upper quartile (3.4) is below the 4.0 bar. Delisting after 12 months is the likely outcome.

The 0.71 correlation between doors and Amazon sales (30 brands) does not show that retail drives Amazon. The causation plausibly runs the other way: Saebom added 300 doors only after reaching about $30M on Amazon.

Mooncrest launched retail-first in 450 doors in 2023, was removed in 2025 and lost an estimated $21M, more than Onsoo's whole $18M cap. Amazon-first produced the one scaled success (Saebom), though two of three stayed below $5M.
Source: Onsoo briefing pack (synthetic data); Table 8 (retail analytics firm, 2025, 46 brands), §10 (survey), §11 (Table 9 competitors), §12 (board member memo).

slides.title: A Japan scale-up is safe but small: +$7M revenue and +$1.8M cash by 2030 in a market growing 1.5% a year

paragraphs.text: A Japan scale-up is safe but small: +$7M revenue and +$1.8M cash by 2030 in a market growing 1.5% a year
Safe: J passes every financial guardrail, with peak cash of −$1.05M and group margin of at least 10.1%.
Small: $7M is 4% of group revenue by 2030, in a market growing about 1.5% a year where Onsoo already holds 3.1%.
Off-strategy: it builds nothing towards the board's US ambition, and the pilot's momentum and learning would sit idle for a year.
Cost of choosing A: about $1.8M of Japan cash forgone by 2030, rising to $4.1M against A's 32%-ACoS case. In return Onsoo gets a $26M US business growing about 29% a year.
Not either/or for ever: the bandwidth limit applies to 2027 only, so J can return in the 2028 plan.
Source: Onsoo briefing pack (synthetic data); Table 7 (Option J), §8 (Japan market growth, share), §3 (bandwidth constraint). Working capital for J is not given in the pack and is excluded.

slides.title: Payback by 2030 hinges on advertising efficiency: Amazon-led pays back only if ACoS averages 28.6% or less, about the pilot's level

paragraphs.text: Payback by 2030 hinges on advertising efficiency: Amazon-led pays back only if ACoS averages 28.6% or less, about the pilot's level
Option A cumulative US cash flow at end-2030, $M, by average ACoS and import duty
Plan, 25%: assumes ACoS falls as the brand matures. Nothing in the pack supports this.
Pilot, 28%: Onsoo's own result, but on a small budget.
Benchmark, 32% (26–38%): brands scaling from $5M to $20M on Amazon, which is exactly A's path ($7M → $26M). Costs per click rise as brands bid on broader keywords.
Each ACoS point = $0.67M of cumulative cash by 2030 (2.81M units × $24 × 1%).
So what: treat 2030 payback as at risk. Manage ACoS to 28% or below as a gate, and expect payback to slip beyond 2030 if ACoS tracks the benchmark. The cap and margin floor still hold.
Above zero = cumulative cash back to zero by end-2030 (payback guardrail met)
Source: Onsoo briefing pack (synthetic data); §6 (pilot ACoS), §11 (agency benchmark), §13 (tariff review). Onsoo option model, Option A volumes held at the plan.

slides.title: No route reaches $40M by 2030 within the guardrails; Amazon-led reaches $26M in 2030 and about $40M by 2032 if growth holds near 23% a year

paragraphs.text: No route reaches $40M by 2030 within the guardrails; Amazon-led reaches $26M in 2030 and about $40M by 2032 if growth holds near 23% a year
Recommended: keep the guardrails, re-phase the ambition
Restate the target as “$25M+ US revenue in 2030, on the way to $40M by about 2032”. Option A fits this, with peak cash of $1.9–3.9M.
Alternative: keep $40M in 2030, relax the guardrails
This means accepting at least $21M of peak cash (above the cap), group margin below 8% for three years, and Mooncrest-type risk. Even then B's own plan reaches $37.6M, not $40M.
Our reading: “on the way to $40M revenue by 2030” means $40M in 2030. If the board meant only a trajectory, Option A already satisfies it.
Benchmark: Saebom (Amazon-first, 2022) reached about $30M in its fourth year. A's plan reaches $26.4M in its fourth year (2030), so it is not a conservative plan.
Source: Onsoo briefing pack (synthetic data); §3 (ambition), Tables 5–7, Table 9 (Saebom). 2031–32 is an illustrative extension at 23% a year (2030 growth: 29%), not a forecast.

slides.title: Model approach: all inputs come from the briefing pack; where it was silent we made the choices below and flag them

paragraphs.text: Model approach: all inputs come from the briefing pack; where it was silent we made the choices below and flag them
Amazon contribution/unit = $24 − 15% referral − $5.10 FBA − $3.50 ex-factory − $0.55 freight − 15% duty on ex-factory − ACoS × $24
Retail contribution/unit = $14 wholesale − $3.50 − $0.75 freight − duty − 8% co-op − 4% returns = $7.545
Retail units = doors × units/door/week × 52; Option B Amazon units = Option A × halo
Cash flow = contribution − fixed costs − one-time costs − inventory build
Inventory = four months of landed cost (ex-factory + freight + duty) on each year's units
Group margin = (11.0% × ex-US revenue + US operating profit) ÷ (ex-US + US revenue)
Payback test: cumulative US cash ≥ 0 by end-2030. Cap test: most negative cumulative cash ≥ −$18M
Breakeven ACoS: the average ACoS at which Option A's end-2030 cumulative cash is exactly zero (solved numerically)
Choices made where the pack is silent
“On the way to $40M by 2030” read as $40M revenue in 2030 (p. 15 shows both readings)
Inventory is built in the year volume is sold and not released by 2030; this is conservative for every option
One-time costs (set-up, launch fee, fixtures) are expensed, so they also count in the margin test
New doors sell for the full year they are added, which flatters Option B
Evidence-based ACoS = 32%, the agency median for brands scaling from $5M to $20M; 28% (pilot) shown as the middle case
Onsoo awareness read as below 10% on Table 8's basis: 4% of all buyers, 9% of K-beauty buyers
Option J excludes working capital, which the pack does not give; this flatters J slightly
No discounting, inflation or price changes; FX at KRW 1,380 per $ (only as context)
Stall case: 200k units a year (≈$4.8M, the level of the Amazon-first peers below $5M) at 28% ACoS
Source: Onsoo briefing pack (synthetic data); model code: deliverable/model/onsoo_model.py.

slides.title: The CEO's 2029 national-retail step would cut group margin to 6.0% and drive cumulative US cash to −$13.8M by 2030

paragraphs.text: The CEO's 2029 national-retail step would cut group margin to 6.0% and drive cumulative US cash to −$13.8M by 2030
A + national retail from 2029 (600 doors, 4.6 u/d/w, no halo, ACoS 28%)
Largest US loss the group can absorb
Even at the >20% awareness level (4.6 units/door/week), 600 national doors add $7.5M a year of fixed cost against about $1.1M of retail contribution.
With a 1.3× halo from 2029 the result barely changes: cumulative cash −$12.0M, group margin 6.4% in 2029.
So retail must wait for both awareness and a cheaper format, not just a revenue milestone.
